subtype: Approach: adjusting when the schedule feels like a burden [Revision]
passage: "Papa, I am changing my chart," Kavitha announced, flute case in hand. Hemant looked up. "Why?" "Seven days makes it homework. Yesterday I played badly on purpose so it would finish sooner." "That does not sound like fun." "It is not! So four days: Monday, Tuesday, Thursday, Saturday. The other days I play only what I feel like." "Will you keep to four?" "Yes, and I will tick them." She stuck the new chart over the old one. On Wednesday, with no rule at all, she picked up the flute anyway and played a film tune for ten happy minutes.

qa.q: Which four days did Kavitha choose?
qa.a: Kavitha chose Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday.

qa.q: What was Kavitha feeling about seven-day practice, and what showed it?
qa.a: Resentful and bored, since she played badly on purpose so that it would finish sooner.

qa.q: What could Kavitha do if four days starts to feel like a chore too?
qa.a: Shorten the sessions or vary what she plays, because enjoyment is what keeps her going.

qa.q: How might Hemant see Kavitha's change?
qa.a: With patience and understanding, since he asked questions and let her decide, and he can see she still wants to play.

grounding: A girl finds daily practice makes the hobby a chore, so she cuts it to four days and leaves the others for free play.
